raw_response:
I've been farming these 15 mu for 45 years now. Me and my wife, we're both getting old — I'm 66, and it's just the two of us. We can't work like we used to, but we know this land better than anyone.

This year, I'll keep 12 mu in wheat and then maize, like always. The other 3 mu I'll plant cotton — my wife handles that plot, she's good at the picking and it gives us some cash in the fall.

For the wheat, I plant in mid-October, same as everyone else in the village. You can't be too early or the wheat grows too much before winter, can't be too late or it won't take hold. I buy improved seed from the shop in town, about 7 or 8 kg per mu, costs around 40 yuan each mu. I don't save my own wheat seed anymore — the shop seed is better.

For fertilizer, I put down one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — those big 50 kg bags. Then when the wheat starts jointing, around Qingming time in early April, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. Three years ago I tried using less because fertilizer got expensive, and the wheat turned yellow and thin. Never again. Better to put a bit more than too little. Old Zhang down the road uses even more, but I think what I do is enough. My soil is decent.

Irrigation, I'll water three times: once after planting if it doesn't rain, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Pumping water costs money — every time I start the well, the meter runs — so I don't water more than I need. But three times is what I've always done, and it works.

For the maize, it goes in right after we cut the wheat in mid-June. Sometimes we only have four or five days, so we don't do much tillage — just chop the wheat stubble and plant. I buy hybrid maize seed every year, you can't save hybrid seed. About 2.5 kg per mu, costs around 50 yuan. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg per mu, and then I try to get back and throw another 10 kg of urea when the maize is knee-high. If I'm too busy or the weather's bad, I might skip that second time, but last year I did it and the maize looked better.

Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat in summer. I'll irrigate twice — once after planting if it's dry, and once at the big flare stage. The summer rains usually help us out.

The cotton, I plant in late April. It's only 3 mu, so we can manage it. Cotton needs more spraying — for the bollworm, for the aphids. I use whatever the shop has, usually the cheaper generic stuff. I put down about 35 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, and then another 10 kg of urea when it flowers. Water it twice. The picking is the hard part — my wife and I do it by hand, three or four times through September and October. We don't hire labor for that, too expensive, and anyway who would come pick cotton for us? Everyone's busy with their own fields.

I don't have much cash to spare. I'm old, I don't take risks. If I'm not sure about something, I do what I did last year. Last year was decent — wheat gave me about 800 jin per mu, maize about 900 jin per mu, cotton was okay. This year I expect about the same if the weather holds. Altogether, seed, fertilizer, water, and medicine will cost me about 9,000 yuan, maybe a bit more. That's a lot for two old people, but we have to spend it to eat.
